svg.text: K8b Sealed tub with magnetic pucks — improved
Nothing passes through a wall: magnets behind the front skin drag pucks inside; a turning floor hub; a well that washes during the meal.
10 motion actuators, all dry · 0 dynamic seals
puck Ø190, planned at R50: ≤ 40 N in plane, 6 Nm rotor
T 30 Nm 0–500 rpm · S 1.5 Nm 0–6000 rpm
next meal 12 min after the last hand-over
FRONT VIEW (door dropped into the plinth: you look at the drive wall)
TOP VIEW (drive wall at the bottom)
drive cassette = door, 90 (heads move behind the skin)
1/7 Transport puts a box in the dock above the ceiling; the shutter opens and the box tips: onion halves fall into the press cup on T.
2/7 P1 sets the dicer grid on the cup; T turns the screw, the piston pushes the onion up through the grid: dice slide down the spout into the pan.
3/7 Zone L heats; P2 stirs with the paddle. The pucks move only because magnets behind the front skin drag them.
4/7 P1 lowers the used cup into the well: hot jets wash it while the downdraft pulls the spray down, away from the food.
5/7 The hatch opens; P1 pulls in the pass tray and sets the warm plate on T.
6/7 T turns the plate while P2 pours sauce in an arc; the plate leaves on the pass tray, the hatch closes.
7/7 After the meal (10 min): the drip bar runs a film down the drive wall, P1 squeegees it, ceiling nozzles wash the rest.
